ai.title: Async agents: spawn, messaging, session-aware inputs
ai.summary: New `AsyncAgentManager` tracks spawned agents, routes `send_agent_message` prompts, and injects pending messages into `runAgentStep` tool results when `ASYNC_AGENTS_ENABLED` is true. `live-user-inputs.ts` splits `endUserInput` from new `cancelUserInput`, adds `sessionConnections` map, and requires `sessionId` in `checkLiveUserInput` to gate on WebSocket status. `superagent` template registered in `agent-list.ts` using `openrouter_claude_sonnet_4`; `main-prompt.ts` now sets `mainAgentState.agentType`. `ai-sdk.ts` passes `clientSessionId` to all three live-input checks.

eli5.text: The assistant can now dispatch helper assistants to work on tasks in the background while it keeps talking to you, and you (as the person watching) can cancel a question you started typing if a background helper is the one actually responding. Under the hood, a new manager keeps track of every helper that is spawned, routes messages between them, and makes sure each helper only acts when its chat session is still active; meanwhile the code that checks whether your connection is live now requires a session ID and can tell the difference between "stop letting me type" and "I changed my mind, drop what I started." If you looked, you would see multiple assistants moving around in your chat at once, and a single text input box could get cancelled by either you or an assistant without confusing

ai.title: Nullable agentType restored in session state schema
ai.summary: AgentStateSchema now accepts null for agentType. AsyncAgentManager adds non-null assertions to suppress TypeScript errors. Initial session state defaults to null instead of fake 'base' string. Scope covers common types and backend async manager.

eli5.text: When a new conversation starts, the assistant no longer puts in a placeholder name like 'base' for what kind of helper it is supposed to be; it just leaves that spot blank ('null') until the real type gets assigned. That blank value is now allowed by the internal checklist that validates session data (the schema), and the part of the system that runs in the background stops complaining about it by treating the blank as valid. Nothing about the assistant's behavior changes for you, but the system handles the setup phase more cleanly without relying on a fake temporary name.

ai.title: Switch tool calls to XML-JSON mix
ai.summary: Tool call parsing switched from pure XML to a hybrid XML-JSON format. `ai-sdk.ts` now emits JSON-encoded parameters wrapped in XML tags, and `prompt-agent-stream.ts` removes per-template `stopSequences` in favor of global constants. This affects all agent templates and the backend streaming logic.

eli5.text: When you ask an AI agent to do a task, it now formats its internal thinking and tool requests using a mix of JSON and XML tags instead of pure XML. This affects how agent templates like "brainstormer" and "git-committer" handle stopping conditions, switching from template-specific stop sequences to global constants. You'd notice the assistant's internal tool calls look cleaner and more consistent, though the end-user experience of interacting with the agent remains the same.

You don't see anything new by itself, this update just bumps the software's version number from 1.0.434 to 1.0.435, which is how the system keeps track of which version is current. But this version number is the one that gets sent out to you, and it bundles in several changes that do affect you: the assistant can now run multiple specialized helpers at the same time and send messages to them, tool results come through in a more reliable format, and the way agent names are cleaned up has been made more predictable so your own custom names are kept intact. There's also a small fix that lets some internal state fields be empty (null) again, which prevents errors when an agent type isn't set. If you install or update today, you get all of that, the new concurrent helpers, sturdier messaging, and the naming fix, packaged under 1.0.435.

ai.title: Enable async agents
ai.summary: ASYNC_AGENTS_ENABLED set to true in common/src/constants.ts. Allows tool calls to continue executing even when main user input is cancelled. Scope limited to shared core constants.

eli5.text: The assistant can now keep running tasks in the background even if you cancel the main request. This works because the system is set to allow separate background work to continue independently. You would notice that a cancelled command no longer stops a long-running task that was already started. This setting is now turned on, so the behavior applies immediately.

ai.title: superagent template prefers sendagentmessage over spawning
ai.summary: superagent.ts adds send_agent_message to toolNames and injects a prompt directive to prefer messaging existing agents over spawning new ones. This reduces redundant agent creation for similar tasks. Scope limited to backend/src/templates/agents/superagent.ts.

eli5.text: Starting today, the assistant will try to send a message to an agent it already created when the task looks similar, instead of automatically spinning up a brand-new agent every time. If you happen to see the assistant at work, you might notice it referring back to a previous agent rather than spawning a new one for closely related tasks. This only applies to the backend template that defines how the assistant picks and manages helper agents, so casual users won't notice any new buttons or settings.

ai.title: knowledge.md adds Bun testing best practices
ai.summary: Added Bun Testing Best Practices section to knowledge.md. Mandates `spyOn()` over `mock.module()` for function mocking to ensure test isolation and easier restoration. `mock.module()` is restricted to entire module replacement scenarios.

eli5.text: The engineering team added a set of rules to their internal testing guide that tells everyone how to write automated tests the right way. If you peeked at their testing notes, you would see a clear recommendation to prefer one mocking technique that is easy to turn off after each test, instead of another that can leak settings between tests and is harder to clean up. The new section is backed by real examples copied from their own test files, showing exactly how the preferred technique is used in practice. This is housekeeping on the team's internal best-practices doc, so it does not change anything an outside user would encounter.

ai.title: Remove agent spawn reminder from base prompt
ai.summary: Removed the system instruction block prompting agent spawning (file picker, thinker, reviewer) from `backend/src/templates/base-prompts.ts`. This internal cleanup eliminates redundant guidance in the base prompt template. The change affects only the backend prompt generation logic.

eli5.text: The assistant no longer receives a built-in reminder telling it to ask for help from helper tools (a file searcher, a thinking tool, and a code reviewer) before it starts working. This is purely an internal cleanup: it only removes that reminder from the instructions the system prepares behind the scenes, so nothing you see day to day should change.

ai.title: Rename agent template description field to purpose
ai.summary: The `description` field in `AgentTemplate` and `ProgrammaticAgentTemplate` types is renamed to `purpose`. This change propagates through backend agent implementations, dynamic agent loading, and shared constants in `common/src/constants/agents.ts`. Existing JSON templates and code referencing the old field name will fail validation or type checks until updated.

eli5.text: You won't see a flashy new button or faster loading screen because of this change. The development team quietly renamed an internal label that describes what each helper assistant is for, it used to be called "description" and is now called "purpose" in every template that defines an assistant. This is like changing the column name in an address book from "Notes" to "Reason I Know Them" without changing any of the actual contact details. Any custom helper assistants or setup files you built yourself that still use the old label will now cause errors until you update them to use the new name, which is part of keeping the system running smoothly behind the scenes.

ai.title: Reenable CI integration tests
ai.summary: Uncommented test-integration job in .github/workflows/ci.yml. Runs integration tests across npm-app, backend, and common packages. Increased timeout to 15 minutes and reduced retries to 3 attempts.

eli5.text: The system has turned back on a set of automatic checks that make sure the main app, the server, and shared code still work correctly together. These checks run behind the scenes whenever the team updates the software, and they will now try harder (up to three attempts) if something briefly fails. You won't see anything different day-to-day, but the team can now catch breaking bugs faster before they affect features.

ai.title: Fix build
ai.summary: CLI agent listing reads `purpose` instead of `description` from `AGENT_PERSONAS` metadata in `npm-app/src/cli.ts`. Troubleshooting docs update example agent config `purpose` field placeholder text.

eli5.text: When you list the built-in helper profiles from the command line, they now show up using their short purpose label instead of a longer description line, so the list matches what the documentation examples tell you to expect. This also fixes the matching documentation example so its placeholder text matches the actual field name the program reads, preventing confusion when someone copies the example to build their own profile. No new behavior or access is added today; it is just a behind-the-scenes alignment so the listing and the guide stay consistent.

ai.title: Enable typecheck for backend tests
ai.summary: Removed `**/*.test.ts` from `exclude` in `backend/tsconfig.json`. Backend test files now undergo typechecking. Ensures type safety in test suites.

eli5.text: Your assistant will notice that the backend team has enabled type checking for their test files. This means that test files are now checked for type errors at build time, which previously were excluded from type checking. This change improves the reliability and type safety of the backend test suites, helping catch potential bugs before they reach production.

ai.title: Remove test exclusions from backend and common tsconfig
ai.summary: Typecheck now covers test files in backend and common packages by removing explicit test exclusion patterns from tsconfig.json. This ensures dynamic-agent-template-schema and agent-template-path-validation tests are included in static analysis. Affects backend/tsconfig.json and common/tsconfig.json.

eli5.text: The system now runs its safety checks on all the behind-the-scenes verification tests, not just most of them. Anyone looking at the system's built-in checks would notice that previously skipped tests are now being reviewed for errors. This means the checks are slightly more thorough starting today.

ai.title: Evals tsconfig includes test files for typecheck
ai.summary: evals/tsconfig.json drops `**/*.test.ts` and `**/*.spec.ts` from `exclude`, so evals typecheck now covers `evals/swe-bench.test.ts`. Previously evals test files were skipped during typecheck, leaving type errors in them undetected. Scope limited to evals tsconfig; no runtime or CLI behavior change.

eli5.text: Internal test scripts for the assistant's grader now get fully checked for mistakes, so developers catch broken helper files before they cause failures. Previously, the system skipped type-checking those test files during setup, leaving issues undetected. You wouldn't see this change in everyday use, but it tightens behind-the-scenes quality control for anyone contributing internal evaluation code.

ai.title: npm-app typecheck covers tests
ai.summary: Removed test exclusions from `npm-app/tsconfig.json`. `include: ["src/**/*.ts"]` now covers test files. Fixes typecheck for npm-app.

eli5.text: The developer tool that checks for errors in the npm app now also checks the app's test files, which were previously skipped during this check. This affects the engineering team building the npm app, who will catch more potential issues before code is shipped. If you were on that team, you would notice that mistakes in the test files now get flagged right away instead of slipping through. This fix is live today.

ai.title: Silence Infisical logs in dev wrapper
ai.summary: The `.bin/bun` script now executes `infisical run` with the `--silent` flag and sets `INFISICAL_DISABLE_UPDATE_CHECK=true`. This change suppresses verbose Infisical output and skips version checks to reduce CLI overhead and speed up startup times for local development. The update is documented in `knowledge.md` under the Infisical wrapper section.

eli5.text: When you start your tools during local development, the secret-loading step that used to print extra messages now stays quiet and skips checking for updates. You will see fewer lines of text scroll by when launching the development server, and startup will feel slightly faster because it no longer pauses to verify whether a newer version is available. This is live today for anyone running the development setup on this machine.

ai.title: Include test files in typecheck
ai.summary: Removed test file exclusion patterns from tsconfig.json in packages/bigquery, packages/billing, packages/code-map, packages/internal, and scripts. This ensures .test.ts and .spec.ts files are now included in type checking. Internal OpenRouter AI SDK tests were also updated to align with this change.

eli5.text: The project's safety checks now look at a wider range of files. Previously, the automated checker that scans for code mistakes ignored test files during its regular sweep. Now, those same test files are included in the automatic review. This means more of the project's code gets reviewed at once, catching potential problems earlier in the development process. You wouldn't see this directly, but it helps prevent certain types of errors from slipping through.

ai.title: Fix type errors in OpenRouter usage accounting tests
ai.summary: OpenRouter usage accounting tests switched from vitest to bun:test. Semicolons removed across test files to match Bun linter style. Fixes type errors in packages/internal/src/openrouter-ai-sdk.

eli5.text: The system that tracks how much you're paying for OpenRouter usage now runs checks using a different testing tool, which means some behind-the-scenes validation files were reformatted. To you, this likely looks like nothing new or different. This change only affects the internal verification process used by programmers and doesn't update features, pricing, or functionality you interact with.
